title: END-TO-END MODELLING OF THE RADIATION HARDNESS ASSURANCE PROCESS - EXPRO+
description: Objectives: To develop an integrated software toolkit to assess the relative contributions to overall errors and uncertainties in the radiation hardness assurance process and estimate the true risk of failures. Description: The current process for Radiation Hardness Assurance (RHA) attempts to ensure compliance to mission robustness, reliability and availability with respect to radiation. This includes a range of measures addressed at different stages of the process. environment models are often applied with confidence levels and margins which in isolation may not sufficiently mitigate risk, the transport of radiation through shielding can incorporatea great deal of hidden margin (depending on the level of detail of the radiation model) but this can also be reduced to near-zero through detailed analysis and effects in components based on test data are highly susceptible to component specifics combined with other degradation parameters and temperature variations. Given this myriad of factors the true risk of component failure is not easy to discern. This activity shall address Radiation Hardness Assurance (RHA) as an integrated approach from radiation environment modelling to component acceptance to determine true risk levels for the end-to-end process. This shall include assessment of the probabilities of component failure for various environments using different methods for capturing environmental variability, radiation model fidelity and uncertainties in component test data and related statistical approaches. This shall be able to incorporate a digital representation of the spacecraft for radiation transport, test data for components and a range of orbital environments thereby spanning multiple disciplines in spacecraft design and quality assurance and extracting benefits from adopting a Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) approach. The system shall incorporate estimates of errors and uncertainties at each step of the process to derivean estimate of the true risk of failure. This activity shall encompass the following tasks: - Investigate the requirements and definition of process by consultation with radiation experts in industry as well as at ESA - Establish the use cases and collect relevant radiation effects data to test in the software; - Design of the software architecture leveraging existing assets to link orbits, environments, propagation and effects; - Develop algorithms to propagate uncertainties through the different steps of the RHA process;- Derivation of "true risk" estimates and comparison with current approaches; - Make recommendations for the maturation of this integrated (MBSE) approach Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT FOR HIGH THROUGHPUT OPTICAL COHERENT TRANSCEIVERS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.008) ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to de-risk high throughput (100-200 Gbps), cross-atmospheric optical communication fordirect to Earth (DTE) and feeder-links. The second objective is to collectstatistics on link quality and availability to support the design of high throughput optical space/ground links.Targeted Improvements:To demonstrate 10x higher throughput than the currently available optical transceivers for space applications from VLEO and LEO.Description:The objective of the activity is to de-risk developments of > 100 Gbps coherent transceivers used for the high throughput cross-atmospheric optical communication for direct to Earth (DTE) andfeeder-links. The activity will consist of the procurement of a cubesat with excellent body pointing capabilities in the order of a few tens of microradians to carry an optical communication payload.It will include an optical communication terminal with two 100-200 Gbps coherent transceivers (Tx and Rx), optical amplifiers and a modem. The development also includes hardware to be installedin an optical ground station to receive and transmit data towards the satellite. Estimated duration is 24 months(12 months development + 12 months IoE).

title: COHERENT RECEIVER TECHNOLOGIES FOR BEYOND-EARTH COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.002) EXPRO+ ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop receiver technologies based on coherent detection of pulse-position modulated (PPM) signals for bidirectional inter-spacecraft links targeting distances above 1.5AU. The feasibility shall be demonstrated through a laboratory breadboard. A beyond-Earth pointing, acquisition and tracking strategy shall be investigated.Targeted Improvements:Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement and increased data rate compared to Geiger mode detection using avalanche photo-receivers.Description:The sensitivity and data rate of the high photon efficiency (HPE) optical communication can be significantly increased by coherent detection of pulse-position modulation. A laboratory breadboard will demonstrate the suitability of coherent reception for inter-spacecraft communications targeting link distances above 1.5 AU, comparing the performance with the current state of art. The activity shall perform a trade-off analysis, performance simulation and the development of a laboratory demonstration. It is expected to improve the resilience on background light, since coherentcommunications are more robust to interference from undesired light sources. Furthermore, this activity will contribute to building the technology required for interplanetary networks supporting human exploration, commercial and scientific missions.
